notes: The built-in device package is first-party code in its own repository, not a vendored third party. It is pinned here because the installer ships a package this repository no longer builds, so the exact bytes must be named and verified rather than assumed.

It is not built from source here because it references the plugin SDK as its own submodule. Building it inside WSGM's solution would put two WSGM.Device.Sdk projects in one build, from two pins free to drift apart.

The archive is what `wsgm-device pack` produced, already validated by the pinned Device Lab in its own repository. WSGM validates the expanded tree again before staging: a package is only as trustworthy as the last validator that saw the exact bytes being shipped.

A release tag is mutable: re-pushing one re-runs its release workflow and replaces the asset with a fresh build, which is never byte-identical. That is a breaking change for every consumer pinning by digest. Prefer a new version over re-tagging.

component.notice: The package carries its own LICENSE.txt, PROVENANCE.md and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.
component.glyphFilesNote: Package validation treats glyph artwork as optional, so a package that lost it passes every gate and simply renders Valve's default glyphs. This count makes that a build failure instead. Update it only when the package deliberately ships a different number.
